name: spatial_nav_auto_scroll_container
description: SPATIAL NAVIGATION CONTAINMENT under `auto` (9a-i-b-i, css-nav-1): a scroll container (overflow: auto) is a spatial navigation container without any `spatial-navigation-contain` declaration. #f1 sits top-left INSIDE the box (centre 40,25); #f2 lower and to the right inside it (centre 100,105: inside azul's 90-degree down cone, cross 60 <= along 80, but scoring 80 + 3*60 = 260); #out sits directly below the box, aligned with #f1 (centre 40,175: score 150). Without containment the better-scoring #out wins; with containment ArrowDown from #f1 must land on #f2, the only candidate inside the innermost container. The last ArrowDown from #f2 finds nothing inside and must escape outward to #out (centre 40,175 is in #f2's cone: cross 60 <= along 70). The geometry is pinned to the resolver's cone-and-weight rule on purpose: a candidate outside the cone is not a candidate at all. Tab focuses #f1 first (it is first in tab order).

css: #box { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 260px; height: 130px; overflow: auto; background: gainsboro; }
.item { position: absolute; width: 60px; height: 30px; background: silver; font-family: "Azul Mock Mono"; font-size: 20px; }
